options.description: Issues are kept in a file for later reuse. Nothing is fixed or rerun automatically. Recommended: You asked that issues be written to a file that you can later re-use, which describes keeping them for later rather than fixing them on the spot.
options.label: Only write the issue to a file (Recommended)

options.description: After each run, plumb fixes the issues on a branch and runs the benchmark again, up to a set number of rounds.
options.label: Fix each issue on a branch, then rerun

payload.question:
When plumb evaluate runs and the model finds an issue, should plumb act on it itself (fix it on a branch and run the benchmark again), or should it only write the issue to a file for you to use later?

You said on 2026-10-21: "when ever Haiku finds issue, it writes into a file that we can later re-use to improve reliability of plumb"
payload.text: Evaluate just documents the issues. but then debug is called to work on those issues, and ensure plumb compliant merge of the fixes. Of course it should come back to the user with question tool when fixing implies changing the intent
